matches.quote: The claim of "optical melting" rests on a fixed-amplitude threshold and on a heating check that cannot reach the electron temperature... bounds the lattice temperature only
Compare the WP slope and curvature with the RP-umklapp data from the same spectra, plotted on a common density axis... Fig. 2d only overlays theory curves
The theory for WPs is a single-oscillator (Einstein) model, while the WC has a gapless phonon continuum... A sideband coupled to an acoustic phonon continuum would generally be broad
The Methods state a "single-gate scan", while Fig. 1a shows two gates and the density formula includes both. Please state exactly which gate was swept
Show whether the WP splitting extrapolates to zero at the onset of doping... at the lowest densities... extracted WP energies against n with uncertainties are not shown
If WPs are AP-plus-WC-phonon states, they should disappear where the WC melts... the umklapp nearly vanishes at ~4000 nW, yet the WP is said to "remain robust"
Their observation in at least one more device, and at several spots on this one, with the spread in n_c, a and the WP-AP splitting, is needed
With kappa = 4.5 and m_e = 0.4 m0, the reported melting at r_s ~ 12 is about three times below the clean-limit value (~31-38).
The hBN thicknesses and the gate-to-sample distances are not given... They also determine whether gate screening matters... changes both the melting density and the WP stiffness.
the measurement is time-integrated over the pulse itself... separate the pump and probe (spectrally or in time, for example with a weak delayed probe)

notes: C7 is marked 'partly' because P15 challenges the anomalously high melting density (r_s ~ 12 with m_e = 0.4 m_0) relative to theoretical expectations rather than specifically contrasting WSe2 with MoSe2. C12 is marked 'partly' because P20/P21 point out that the measurements are time-integrated without time-resolved pump-probe separation and P9 questions whether the title claim to reveal WC dynamics follows, without directly framing it around CW vs time-resolved terminology. P12 and P14 are section-heading artifacts from the prompt list and are graded as generic/minor.
